title: Raw Material Safety in Juice Production
reason: The transcript details multiple principles and practices for minimizing microbial contamination in fresh produce, which is relevant to food safety.

tasks.task: Explain the importance of agricultural and manufacturing practices for minimizing microbial contamination in fresh produce.

subtasks.text: Note that the safety and quality of the final juice is dependent on the safety and quality of the raw material.
Identify that raw materials can include fruits and vegetables and various types of water and additives throughout the process.
Indicate how the environment, both in and around growing fields and packing houses, can influence the safety and quality of raw materials.
Mention that microbial contamination of produce can occur at any point during its production.
Discuss the commitment required from farmers and their workers to reduce microbial risks.
Highlight that raw materials for fruit and vegetable juices are produced in many different geographical areas.
List examples of raw materials coming from different parts of the United States.
Point out that raw materials can be of varying shapes and sizes and may arrive at the processor in different forms.

tasks.task: Describe the principles and recommended practices to minimize microbial food safety hazards in fresh produce.

subtasks.text: Explain principle one - prevention of microbial contamination is favored over reliance on corrective actions after contamination has occurred.
State principle two - growers, packers, or shippers should use good agricultural and manufacturing practices in areas over which they have control.
Outline principle three - produce can become microbiologically contaminated at any point along the farm to table food chain.
Mention principle four - water quality and its source dictate the potential for contamination when water comes into contact with produce.
Discuss principle five - managing practices using animal manure or municipal biosolid waste to minimize microbial contamination.
Highlight principle six - worker hygiene and sanitation practices play a critical role in minimizing microbial contamination.
